tokenizer_mocks.note: These are hand-written tokenizer stand-ins, not Qwen tokenizer metadata. They fix one input shape each so that a one-to-many selection policy has to declare what it keeps. No result here is evidence about the real Qwen3-0.6B or Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct tokenizers.
tokenizer_mocks.encode_rule: greedy longest-prefix match over vocab; equal-length prefix matches resolve to the smallest token id
tokenizer_mocks.decode_rule: decode([id]) returns the vocab string verbatim

preservation_criteria.exact_lexeme: the selected LLM token, stripped of surrounding whitespace, must equal the required lexeme exactly
preservation_criteria.complete_content: the selected LLM token, stripped of surrounding whitespace, must equal the full stripped text of the SLM token

fixtures.why_this_role: In 'x is not y' the negation is carried by one lexeme. If the aligned position keeps only the separating space, the aligned sequence loses the negation word at that position.

A year is only meaningful as a whole. Any single candidate here is a two-digit fragment, so no choice under either strategy can keep the date intact; the point is to record what the source actually does rather than to assume a tie is handled.
A 1-to-1 mapping has nothing to select, so it must be unaffected by the strategy; this isolates any observed difference to the 1-to-many branch.

Both first and longest keep the complete negation lexeme not when it occurs before a trailing space. This controls the position of the same required lexeme; it does not require preservation of whitespace.
